R17 on the EC channel), so the EZO-pH module cannot communicate over I2C. pH measurement/dosing fails while the equally-designed EC channel still works, i.e. the board does not behave as the intended symmetric design.",

anomalies.observed: C61 is a 22µF ceramic capacitor (value "22μ", footprint "Coert-Vonk:CAP X7R 22μF ±10 10V 1206") connected between the isolated pH I2C data net /SDA_{pH} (C61 pin1, together with M2 pin3 RX/SDA and U3 pin18 SDA_1) and the isolated pH supply net /V_{pH} (C61 pin2). The symmetric isolated EC channel has no such capacitor; instead it has the pull-up resistor R17 (2.2k) from /SDA_{EC} to /V_{EC}.
anomalies.expected: The isolated pH SDA line (like the EC SDA line) should be terminated only by a 2.2k pull-up to /V_{pH} (cf. R17 on the EC side); a 22µF capacitor from SDA to V_pH is not a valid part for that position. The EC channel (R17 on SDA, R19 on SCL) shows the intended symmetry.

evidence.quote: each with its own isolated supply (`/V_pH`, `/V_EC`) and isolated ground (`/GNDISO_pH`, `/GNDISO_EC`)

anomalies.impact: A 22µF capacitor from the isolated pH I2C data line to the isolated 5V rail puts an enormous capacitive load on SDA (and the matching pH SDA pull-up resistor is absent, cf. R17 on the EC channel), so the EZO-pH module cannot communicate over I2C. pH measurement/dosing fails while the equally-designed EC channel still works, i.e. the board does not behave as the intended symmetric design.

parsed.summary: The design is intended to treat the isolated pH and EC I2C channels symmetrically, but the pH channel's SDA net /SDA_{pH} is loaded with a 22µF capacitor C61 to /V_{pH} (and its matching 2.2k pull-up is absent), whereas the EC channel correctly uses a 2.2k pull-up (R17); this would break I2C communication with the EZO-pH module.
